title: Where the time goes: one cross-continent call costs ~300 in-DC round trips
caption: Each rung is roughly 10–1 000× the one before. Count the slow hops on a request path, not the fast ones.

messages.label: read RAM ≈ 100 ns
messages.note: Main memory: about 10 million reads fit in one second.

messages.label: random read ≈ 100 µs
messages.note: 1 000× slower than RAM. A spinning disk seek would be another 100× on top (~10 ms).

messages.label: GET ≈ 0.5 ms round trip
messages.note: A network hop inside one data center. A remote cache still beats reading the database.

messages.label: call ≈ 150 ms round trip
messages.note: Speed of light plus routing. Two of these and a user-facing budget of 300 ms is gone.

messages.label: response
messages.note: Hence: keep chatty calls inside one region, and put content near users (CDN, regional replicas).
